additional_considerations.rationale: Another crystal arthritis that often involves the knees and wrists, but it is usually seen in patients older than 60.
Typical in young women and often affects the knee, but it is usually preceded by migratory polyarthralgias, and the characteristic pustular rash is absent.
Sudden onset, usually knee or wrist, mostly S aureus; key risk factors (previous joint damage, IV drug use) are absent.
Insidious onset, brief stiffness and minimal inflammation do not fit; it spares the wrist and MCP joints and has no constitutional symptoms.

source_issues: Internal inconsistency in the script: p005 says rest and Tylenol 'help a little bit', p029 says Tylenol 'is not working anymore'. Both are kept as stated (f007, f043, flagged).
Exam line e006 records 'active bowel sounds four times per minute'; this may be a garbled 'x4 quadrants'. Kept neutral in x009.
The raw sheet's Patient Description ('divorced with two daughters') is not in the parsed source fields; marital status was added to persona.acting_notes, not as a patient fact.
The note's SH says 'on weekends drinks more'; the patient only says she does not count on weekends (p034). Patient facts keep her wording.

Gold rank-1 history finding 'Occasional alcohol use' understates the script (2-4 beers a week plus uncounted weekend drinking). Gold 'Monoarticular joint pain' sits beside a history of chronic wrist and finger pain.
The note exam reports wrists within normal limits bilaterally, while the patient reports constant wrist pain and stiffness (p008); this is history vs exam, not changed.
annotator_notes: Opening fact is the chief-complaint answer 'Left knee pain.'
p024 and p031 overlap on the C-sections: f036 keeps the two daughters (ob_gyn) and f037 combines delivery mode and the ages at the C-sections (psh), to avoid a paraphrase duplicate.
p014 is split into fatigue (f019) and lack of energy to work (f020, functional); the 6-month duration is applied to both because it ends the single sentence.
p020 'Have you ever had seizures?' gives 'never had seizures' (historical); weakness and numbness are current denials.
p030 'None' (no other medical problems) is not treated as contradicting the toe episode (p008) or gonorrhea (p044), which the patient reports elsewhere.
f045 (mother has rheumatoid arthritis) names the rank-2 gold diagnosis; it is legitimate family history and not the rank-1 diagnosis, so leakage_check stays 'none'.
Doorway vitals and the note ('WNL except for low-grade fever') agree: temperature 99.9°F.
